summary: You take SOC 1, 170, 180A and 180B, one foundation course in each of three areas, a methods course you move in by hand, the WIM and a capstone (SOC 202 with an honors thesis, or SOC 204A with a capstone paper), and Social Science electives (at most 10 units from Anthropology, Communication, Economics, Political Science or Psychology) for 60 units. S and CR grades count; a course taken for a letter grade needs a C or better. The Data Science, Markets and Management subplan is optional; its seven additional courses are moved in by hand. Honors admission, the thesis grade and the colloquium are checked by hand.

program.why: Grading: "Grades of S or CR are allowable. When students take classes for a letter grade, the student should earn a C or better or obtain a written exception." A written exception is moved in by hand.

No list: the course is moved in.

YVrurEDG.why: "In addition to the Core classes and the Foundation classes, the Data Science, Markets and Management subplan requires seven additional courses, as follows: Four additional Sociology (SOC) courses - 16 units; Two additional Computer Science, Math, Statistics, or Quantitative Social Science Courses - 8 units; One additional Sociology or Social Science elective - 4 units". The text does not say whether these also count as the major's Social Science electives (which only bring the major to 60 units), so a person confirms the seven courses and they may be courses the major already counts.
